summary: A 1964 R-6 timber tower in the Flathead National Forest replaced a 1928 tower; its lower stairs came out in 2005, and it is staffed in summer.

facts.design: Treated-timber tower with a flat-roofed R-6 cab, built 1964 to replace a 1928 30-foot tower

staffing.status: Staffed in summer (firelookout.com); a Forest Service employee now works at the lookout (Flathead Beacon, 2026)

access.note: Lower stairs were removed in 2005 for vandalism and liability reasons. NHLR does not say they were replaced, so do not assume the tower can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: On a ridge west of Mount Baptiste, roughly 25 miles southeast of Hungry Horse, Montana

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Flathead National Forest

corrections.why: firelookout.com describes the present tower as a 30-foot treated timber tower with an R-6 flat cab. The NHLR page gives no height, and nothing in the record supports 3.7 m.

events.note: Site first used for lookout work, with a camp (firelookout.com)

Rehabilitation began after a 2010 Forest Service site assessment; NHLR expected completion in fall 2013
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 11, 2014; nominated by Brian Powell

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR expected the rehabilitation to finish in fall 2013 but already lists volunteer staffing from 2012. The sources here do not settle when the work finished, so the story says the date is unclear.

notes_for_editor: Stair status after rehabilitation is unconfirmed; NHLR says the lower stairs were removed in 2005 and no source I read says they were replaced. Completion year is unclear: NHLR says fall 2013 and also lists volunteer staffing from 2012. Search summaries (not cited, not verified) said the tower returned to service in 2012 and was staffed by volunteers 2012-2017 and by a Forest Service employee from 2018. The Forest Service PDF named in the brief (stelprd3792970.pdf) returned 404 and was not used. The NHLR page links a Bob Marshall Wilderness Complex newsletter on the renovations; it is a lead for the stair and completion question. The height correction (3.7 m to 9.1 m) rests on firelookout.com alone. Coordinates match NHLR. The Flathead Beacon source spells the lookout 'Baptise' (typo kept in the quote).
